## What I changed

next.config.ts — enabled partialPrefetching: true (alongside the existing cacheComponents: true). This is required for the App Shell vs. per-link prefetch distinction that the task relies on. Without it, prefetch() has no effect and a default <Link> would fetch the whole route.

app/product/page.tsx — moved the related-products fetch out of the page body and into a deferred RelatedProducts async component wrapped in <Suspense>. That component calls await prefetch() (imported from next/cache) before reading getRelatedProducts(). Per the [prefetch() reference](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/prefetch.md), this keeps the subtree out of the route's App Shell (what every default <Link> prefetches) while still including it in a per-link prefetch and on navigation. The <Suspense> fallback ("Loading related products…") is what the default prefetch sees instead; the real list streams in once a per-link prefetch or the navigation resolves it.

app/page.tsx — set prefetch={true} on the featured-product link. Per the [Optimizing prefetching guide](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/optimizing-prefetching.md), this opts that one link into per-link prefetching, which resolves the cached related-products content before the click. So navigating from the featured-product link shows the list immediately, with no fallback.

## Why prefetch() and not navigation()

I considered navigation() from next/cache, but per its [reference](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/navigation.md) it excludes content from both the App Shell and per-link prefetches — so prefetch={true} on the featured link would not have made the related products ready before the click. prefetch() is the primitive that keeps content out of the default prefetch while still letting a <Link prefetch={true}> resolve it ahead of time, which is exactly the two-sided requirement.

## Verification

- npx tsc --noEmit → exit 0, no errors.
- npm run build → exit 0. Build output confirms "Cache Components enabled" and "Partial Prefetching enabled", /product prerenders as static (Revalidate 1h / Expire 1d, matching cacheLife('hours')), with no instant-navigation validation errors — which confirms the <Suspense> boundary around the prefetch() call is correctly placed.

One note: prefetching only runs in production (next start), not in next dev, so the difference is observable via npm run build && npm start, not in the dev server.

20 	Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

Links to the same route reuse that App Shell.

19 	
20 	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21

23 	
24 	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25 	
26 	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.

30
